ai.description: The Netravali leaping frog is a small, slender amphibian (25–30 mm) with a brown dorsum and dark lateral bands. It features a pointed snout and elongated hind limbs adapted for jumping.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Indirana salelkari* is best distinguished by the distinct, pale-colored longitudinal stripe running along the center of its back, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Netravali Leaping Frog inhabits the moist, evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, specifically thriving near rocky streams at mid-to-high elevations.
ai.behavior: The Netravali leaping frog is primarily nocturnal, actively hunting for small insects among leaf litter and rocky streams under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Indirana salelkari* breeds during the monsoon, laying terrestrial egg clutches on wet rock surfaces near streams, which later hatch into semi-aquatic tadpoles.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Netravali leaping frog is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically found in the Netravali Wildlife Sanctuary of Goa at mid-elevations.
ai.callDescription: The Netravali Leaping Frog emits a series of high-pitched, short, pulsed chirps, typically heard while perched on mossy rocks near fast-flowing streams in forest habitats.
